definition: Encoding images compactly — classical codecs (JPEG) and learned neural compressors that now rival handcrafted standards.
details: Encoding images compactly — classical codecs (JPEG) and learned neural compressors that now rival handcrafted standards.

explainer.lead: Image compression encodes images compactly, spanning classical codecs like JPEG and learned neural compressors that now rival handcrafted standards. It matters because it reduces the cost of storing and transmitting digital images.

tiers.eli5: It is packing a picture into a smaller file so it takes less space or sends faster, like folding clothes tightly into a suitcase.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose lossless compression for archival, medical imaging, technical drawings, clip art, and comics, and lossy methods for natural photographs where minor fidelity loss is acceptable. Pitfall: lossy methods at low bit rates introduce compression artifacts; lossy compression with negligible differences may be called visually lossless.
tiers.paperLevel: Data compression applied to digital images. Lossy methods may use transform coding, most commonly the Discrete Cosine Transform; lossless is preferred where fidelity must be preserved.

explainer.example: A photograph is stored with a lossy DCT-based codec to cut its bit rate substantially, accepting minor, sometimes imperceptible, fidelity loss; an archival medical image instead uses lossless compression.

image.alt: Image compression — Reduction of image size to save storage and transmission costs
